key_concepts: Animals are classified as vertebrates or invertebrates based on the presence of a backbone
Vertebrates include fish, reptiles, mammals, birds, and amphibians.
Fish are aquatic vertebrates with gills, fins, and scales.
Reptiles have dry scaly skin and hatch from eggs.
Mammals have fur or hair, give birth to live young, and feed their young with milk from ma
Birds have wings, beaks, and claws and many build nests.
Amphibians live on land and in water and eat insects.
Invertebrates lack a backbone and include groups such as poriferans, cnidarians, flatworms
Poriferans have pores, cnidarians include hydras and jellyfish, and echinoderms are spiny.
Mollusks have soft bodies and some have shells.
Vertebrate groups differ in breathing organs and reproduction methods.
